register: # SOURCE: ABB/FIMER 'Modbus RTU Register Map - Version GT05, TRIO-20.0(27.6)-TL-OUTD (rev 1.6, 2016)' (vendor document). ABB's tables give 1-based Modbus Data Addresses and state that the PDU address on the wire is one less, so every CSV register here is the table address minus 1 (each note shows the table address).

# FUNCTION CODES: measurements are input registers (FC04). The holding map (FC03 read, FC06/FC16 write; broadcast writes are supported) has the heartbeat and grid measures plus ABB's documented controls, marked RW with ABB's range for write validation. Whether anything can actually be written is decided by the app's gates (transport write_enabled and the per-register W toggle in the web UI). Power management has two independent blocks: block 1 (holding 189-226, older) and block 2 (holding 500-515, plant controller); configure 500-505 before sending a block-2 set point.

note: table 180; ABB read/write control. 0 = on, 1 = off. Writable only if the Remote on/off function is enabled in the inverter.
table 181; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to reset the alarms manually; the register then returns to 0. Writable only if the Reset by-hand function is enabled in the inverter.

documented_name: Block 1 Power Ramping Interval (Permanent and Dynamic)
note: table 190; ABB read/write control. Packed value: low byte N (1 s step 0-250, 4 s step 0-62), high byte M (10 ms step 0-99); T = N x step + M x 10 ms (ABB note 12). Default 15 (60 s).
table 191; ABB read/write control. Countdown used for dynamic active/reactive commands.
table 198; ABB read/write control. Only 0, 128, 256 or 384 are valid (ABB note 13): high byte 0 = 4 s step / 1 = 1 s step, low byte 0 = slope / 128 = duration. Default 0.

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Power Factor Set Point
note: table 200; ABB read/write control. ABB range -1.0..-0.8 or 0.8..1.0 (negative = over-excited, positive = under-excited). Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Power Factor Set Point
note: table 202; ABB read/write control. ABB range -1.0..-0.8 or 0.8..1.0 (negative = over-excited, positive = under-excited). Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).
table 205; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to reset PF to 1; the register then returns to 0.

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Active Power Set Point
note: table 210; ABB read/write control. Percentage of nominal power in 1% steps. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires.

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Active Power Set Point
note: table 212; ABB read/write control. Percentage of nominal power in 1% steps. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation.
table 215; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to reset active power to 100% of nominal; the register then returns to 0.

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Reactive Power Set Point (PF)
note: table 220; ABB read/write control. ABB range -0.8..0.8 (negative = over-excited, positive = under-excited). Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Reactive Power Set Point (PF)
note: table 222; ABB read/write control. ABB range -0.8..0.8 (negative = over-excited, positive = under-excited). Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation. IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).

documented_name: Block 1 Dynamic Reactive Power Set Point (%)
note: table 225; ABB read/write control. ABB range -80..80 %; negative = over-excited. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires.

documented_name: Block 1 Permanent Reactive Power Set Point (%)
note: table 227; ABB read/write control. ABB range -80..80 %; negative = over-excited. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation.
table 299; read-only: 1 = registers 198 and 505 are configurable. Duration mode and the 1 s step need this to be 1
table 300; increments every second, wraps at 65535
table 301; IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first). Returns 0xFFFFFFFF if the inverter does not support it.
table 303; IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).
table 305; IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).
table 307; IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).
table 501; ABB read/write control. Unit of 506, 507, 510 and 511: 0 = per mille, 1 = percent. Default 0.
table 502; ABB read/write control. 0 = dynamic, 1 = permanent. Default 0.

documented_name: Block 2 Power Ramping Interval (Permanent and Dynamic)
note: table 503; ABB read/write control. Packed value: low byte N (1 s step 0-250, 4 s step 0-62), high byte M (10 ms step 0-99); T = N x step + M x 10 ms (ABB note 12). Default 15 (60 s).
table 504; ABB read/write control. Default 2 min.
table 505; ABB read/write control. Only 0, 128, 256 or 384 are valid (ABB note 13): high byte 0 = 4 s step / 1 = 1 s step, low byte 0 = slope / 128 = duration. Default 0.
table 506; ABB read/write control. 0 = PF fixed, 1 = Q fixed. Default 0.

table 508; ABB read/write control. Percent or per mille per register 500. Dynamic: reverts to the default when the timeout register expires.

table 511; ABB read/write control. Percent or per mille per register 500; negative = over-excited. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation.

table 512; ABB read/write control. Percent or per mille per register 500. Permanent: stored in the inverter's memory; ABB warns that writing permanent set points continuously can damage that memory, so use dynamic set points for regulation.

IEEE-754 float, word-swapped (low register first).
table 515; ABB read/write control. Write 1 to force active power back to 100% of nominal; the register then returns to 0.
